title: GroundTruth — Understand your code. Think in systems.
evidenceLabel: Edited walkthrough · real hosted UI captures · synthetic demo account

scenes.title: Understand your code. Think in systems.
scenes.caption: The next change should become your decision.
scenes.narration: AI can produce a working app before its builder understands the system. Even a one-line change can send a beginner back to an assistant to reread the repository. GroundTruth addresses that next-change moment.

scenes.title: From generated software to independent builders
scenes.caption: Build a mental model of the code and architecture.
scenes.narration: The goal is a builder who understands the code and architecture, then practises making a change independently. This edited walkthrough uses real hosted interface captures and a synthetic demonstration account.

scenes.title: Start with a feature, before a filename
scenes.caption: Choose the workflow you want to understand.
scenes.narration: Bring a public GitHub repository and choose a feature to strengthen. Our small study-task project makes the journey easy to inspect. The learner chooses a backend workflow, rather than needing to know which file to open first.

scenes.title: Connect source to system responsibilities
scenes.caption: Follow a request through validation and persistence.
scenes.narration: GroundTruth explains the selected workflow with a beginner overview, reading flow, glossary and visible source at a pinned commit. Where does the request go? Which component validates it? The learner connects individual lines to system responsibilities.

scenes.title: Focus on one concept at a time
scenes.caption: Build a systems view through focused practice.
scenes.narration: A small concept tree links the workflow to focused practice. The learner can strengthen validation before moving on. Muse Spark generates contextual learning content from the selected source and goal, within a consistent interface.

scenes.title: Make the first step approachable
scenes.caption: Project-specific MCQs and tiny coding tasks.
scenes.narration: A beginner can start with an MCQ, then try a tiny coding task. Questions belong to this selected code. The model's suggested answer is still reviewable against the source. A generated explanation is not automatically a fact.

scenes.title: Now the assistant steps aside
scenes.caption: Study help pauses. The first submission is preserved.
scenes.narration: The independent attempt changes the rules. New study assistance pauses while the learner answers. The first submitted response is retained before feedback. The learner can also end an attempt without inventing a completed answer. Outside tools remain beyond GroundTruth's control.

scenes.title: Keep evidence, rather than assume mastery
scenes.caption: Saved attempts connect back to concepts.
scenes.narration: Progress brings the attempt and observed app activity together. The concept index is provisional evidence, not an automatic grade or a validated measure of mastery. The learner decides which project to share with an approved teacher.

scenes.title: Give the teacher something inspectable
scenes.caption: Explicit sharing. Original attempts. Human review.
scenes.narration: The teacher reviews the original attempt and relevant activity. Class enrollment alone does not expose every project. A working AI-built application starts the conversation; the learner's independent attempt adds evidence.

scenes.title: Contextual guidance with explicit boundaries
scenes.caption: Understand the code. Think in systems. Make the next change yourself.
scenes.narration: Meta supplies contextual guidance. GroundTruth on Vercel controls access and learning state, with Supabase preserving the evidence. Our aim is simple: understand the code, think in systems, and make the next change yourself.
